tldr: Two IPOs opened to very different demand: Zetwerk's ₹5,012 Cr issue was 23% subscribed on day one, Tonbo Imaging's ₹852 Cr issue about 4 times.
Flipkart and Udaan both grew revenue in FY26 and lost less money, but Udaan's accounts carry a going-concern warning.
SEBI wants to tighten the rules for small-company (SME) IPOs and is taking public comments until 4 November.
Robotics startup Origin came out of stealth with $20 Mn from Accel and Zacua Ventures.
Globally, 38 startups became unicorns in September, the busiest month of 2026 so far.

stories.title: Origin raises $20 Mn to build construction robots
stories.summary: Origin, a robotics startup that had been working quietly (in 'stealth'), announced $20 Mn of funding co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures. It builds robots that finish walls on construction sites, and will use the money to grow and run trial projects in the US and Europe.
stories.whyItMatters: Construction is a huge industry that still runs mostly on manual labour, so investors are betting robots can take on repetitive site work. Accel backing it signals that big funds see real business, not just research, in physical-world AI.

stories.title: Zetwerk's IPO gets a slow start: 23% subscribed on day one
stories.summary: Zetwerk, a manufacturing marketplace startup, is raising ₹5,012 Cr in its IPO (its first sale of shares to the public). On the first day, bids covered only about 23% of the shares on offer. Large institutional investors (QIBs) showed the most interest, and the issue stays open until 19 October.
stories.whyItMatters: An IPO is how early investors like VCs finally turn their stake into cash. Weak early demand can mean investors think the price is too high, which affects how much those backers make. Many IPOs fill up mostly on the last day, so watch the final number.

stories.title: Defence tech firm Tonbo Imaging's IPO is 4 times subscribed on day one
stories.summary: Tonbo Imaging, which makes imaging technology for defence, is raising ₹852 Cr through its IPO. On day one, investors bid for about four times the shares available. Most of the demand came from wealthy individual and corporate investors (called NIIs).
stories.whyItMatters: Strong demand for a defence tech listing shows public-market investors are excited about this sector. That makes it easier for VCs funding younger defence startups to believe they will have a good way to exit later.

stories.title: Goldman Sachs sells ₹169 Cr of Eternal shares in a block deal
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs sold about 53.4 lakh shares of Eternal (the company behind Zomato and Blinkit) worth roughly ₹169 Cr in one large trade, called a block deal. The shares were sold at a discount to the previous day's closing price, and an affiliate of Bank of America bought them.
stories.whyItMatters: Block deals are how big holders sell a large stake in one go without crashing the share price. Watching who sells and who buys listed startups tells you how professional investors currently value the sector.

stories.title: Fairfax plans to move its Go Digit stake to IDBI Bank
stories.summary: Fairfax Financial has proposed shifting its holdings in Go Digit's insurance businesses to IDBI Bank, and Fairfax India proposed a similar move for its stake in IIFL Capital. This follows Fairfax being chosen as the strategic buyer of IDBI Bank. Regulators still need to approve the plans.
stories.whyItMatters: Go Digit is an insurtech that is now listed on the stock market. Large owners reshuffling their stakes can change who controls a company and how its shares trade, which matters to every other investor in it.

stories.title: Jio says new services, not price hikes, will grow revenue ahead of its IPO
stories.summary: Akash Ambani said Jio plans to earn more from each customer by selling new services rather than raising mobile tariffs. The comments come as Jio gets closer to what is expected to be a record-sized IPO.
stories.whyItMatters: A record IPO sets the mood for the whole market. If it goes well, investors are more willing to buy into other large Indian tech listings, which helps VC-backed companies planning to go public.

stories.title: Flipkart's FY26 revenue nears ₹1.5 lakh Cr as losses shrink
stories.summary: Flipkart Group's total revenue for FY26 grew about 18%, to nearly ₹1.5 lakh Cr, and its loss narrowed slightly to ₹8,468 Cr. But its main shopping business for consumers (the B2C arm) saw revenue fall and losses widen.
stories.whyItMatters: Flipkart is expected to go public eventually. Investors look for a path to profit before an IPO, so a shrinking loss is a good sign, while the weaker consumer business is the part they will question.

stories.title: Udaan grows revenue 13% but its accounts flag a going-concern risk
stories.summary: Udaan, which sells goods wholesale to small shops (B2B e-commerce), grew FY26 revenue by about 13% to ₹5,134 Cr and cut its loss to ₹852 Cr. However, its financial statements carry a 'going-concern' warning, and creditors have started legal proceedings against its parent company abroad.
stories.whyItMatters: A going-concern warning means auditors are unsure the company can keep operating without fresh money. For a VC, that is a red flag that outweighs revenue growth and usually means hard choices: a cheaper new round, a sale, or losses for current investors.

stories.title: Shopify reportedly plans to bring Shop Pay checkout to India
stories.summary: According to sources, Shopify plans to launch Shop Pay, its fast one-click checkout, in India by early 2027, possibly working through local payment partners. That would put it up against Indian checkout startups such as GoKwik and Shopflo.
stories.whyItMatters: When a global giant enters a market, VC-backed local players face a much tougher fight. Investors in GoKwik and Shopflo will watch whether they can hold on to online brands as customers.

stories.title: Swiggy targets the 90% of Indians who have never ordered food online
stories.summary: Swiggy's food delivery CEO Rohit Kapoor said growth will come from people who have never used food delivery, especially price-conscious and younger customers, and from expanding into more cities. He sees AI mainly as a way to make ordering more convenient.
stories.whyItMatters: This is a market-size argument: a business that has only reached 10% of potential users still has lots of room to grow. Judging how big a market really is, and how fast a company can reach it, is a core VC skill.

stories.title: IIT Bombay spinout MumbaiSemi builds RF chips that work with NavIC
stories.summary: MumbaiSemi, a startup that came out of IIT Bombay, has built a programmable radio-frequency (RF) chip that works with India's NavIC navigation satellites as well as other global systems. It wants to become a global supplier of high-quality RF chips.
stories.whyItMatters: Semiconductors are a national priority, and deeptech startups born in university labs are a growing focus for Indian VCs. These companies take longer to build, but can become very hard for competitors to copy.

stories.title: SEBI proposes 10 big changes to SME IPO rules
stories.summary: SEBI, India's stock market regulator, has proposed overhauling the rules for IPOs by small and medium companies (SMEs). The changes cover how companies are valued, profit requirements, how long early shareholders must hold their shares (lock-ins), minimum bid sizes, underwriting and moving up to the main stock exchange. Anyone can comment until 4 November.
stories.whyItMatters: The SME exchange has become an exit route for smaller startups. Stricter rules could make that route harder and slower, which changes how investors plan their exits from small companies.

stories.title: Jio Financial's quarterly profit halves even as revenue jumps 73%
stories.summary: Jio Financial Services earned ₹340 Cr in profit in the July to September quarter, about half of what it made a year earlier, mainly because borrowing costs rose and it received less dividend income. Revenue still grew 73%, led by lending, insurance broking and asset management.
stories.whyItMatters: This is a reminder that revenue growth and profit are different things. In lending businesses, the cost of borrowing money can eat into profits fast, which is exactly what investors check in fintech startups too.

stories.title: 38 new unicorns in September, the busiest month of the year
stories.summary: Thirty-eight startups crossed a $1 billion valuation (became 'unicorns') in September 2026, adding about $71 billion in combined value. Semiconductor, financial services and space technology companies led the list, bringing the total for 2026 to 311 new unicorns.
stories.whyItMatters: The number of new unicorns is a quick health check for venture capital. A busy month suggests investors are confident and willing to pay high prices, especially for chips, fintech and space.

stories.title: Cybersecurity startups raised $6.8B in Q3, mostly in big rounds
stories.summary: Investors put $6.8 billion into cybersecurity startups in July to September 2026, about 50% more than the quarter before. The rise came from larger rounds rather than more deals, and AI-focused security companies took most of the money.
stories.whyItMatters: More money spread over fewer, bigger deals means investors are concentrating on the companies they think will win. It is harder for small new players to raise, but the leaders get a lot of fuel.

stories.title: Chariot raises $10M Series A to help people fight hidden fees
stories.summary: Chariot Claims raised a $10M Series A round led by Silverton Partners. It works with law firms to help consumers bring claims over privacy violations, hidden fees and subscriptions that are hard to cancel.
stories.whyItMatters: A Series A is usually a startup's first large round of outside funding, raised once it has early proof the product works. Legal tech that turns consumer complaints into a business is a niche investors are testing.

stories.title: Stella & Dot founder raises $5M seed for AI marketing startup Marklo
stories.summary: Jessica Herrin, who founded Stella & Dot, raised a $5M seed round led by Forerunner for her new company, Marklo. It helps brands plan marketing campaigns using their own sales, stock and marketing data.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors back repeat founders more easily because they have already built a company once. A seed round is the earliest stage of VC funding, so this is a bet mostly on the founder.

concept.explanation: When a company goes public, it offers a fixed number of new shares, and investors place bids to buy them. 'Subscription' compares how many shares were asked for with how many were on offer. If an IPO is subscribed 1 time, demand exactly matched supply; 4 times means people wanted four times more shares than were available; 23% means only about a quarter of the shares had bids. Bids are counted separately for big institutions (QIBs), wealthy individuals and companies (NIIs) and small retail investors, because each group reads the company differently.
concept.example: Today, Tonbo Imaging's IPO was about 4 times subscribed on day one, while Zetwerk's was only 23% subscribed. Both are still open, and many IPOs see most of their bids arrive on the final day.
